newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian car market seen growing further in March.
newsitem.headline: Italian car market seen growing further in March.

text.p: The sharp rise in new car sales in Italy in February could mark the start of a very good period for the domestic market, auto research body CSP said.
Italian new car registrations rose 21.45 percent to 198,000 vehicles compared with 163,031 in February 1996, official Transport Ministry data showed on Monday.
"In March the growth in sales will be considerably stronger," Centro Studi Promotor said in a statement.
Its latest monthly survey of Italian car dealers showed the percentage of those declaring high levels of orders rising to 85 percent, from 65 percent in January and only six percent last September
The only worry expressed by dealers was that of not having enough new cars available for sale, CSP said.
It said the government's incentive scheme to scrap old cars in exchange for buying new models, introduced in January, "is not only working but is in a phase of full acceleration."
The scheme also seemed to have given a boost to demand in southern Italy which was showing a strong recovery after being hit hard by the car sector crisis which began in 1993.
CSP said orders for new cars linked to the incentive scheme averaged some 49 percent of total orders with this figure rising to 54 percent in the south.
